The annual CPI inflation rate fell from 3.4% to 3.3% in May, below than the median economist projection of 3.4%. According to Econoday, the economist consensus ranged from 3.3% to 3.5%.
On a monthly basis, the overall CPI inflation stalled, decelerating from the prior 0.3% growth and coming in below expectations of 0.1%.
The energy index dropped by 2.0% over the month, driven primarily by a 3.6% decline in the gasoline index.

While Nvidia would diversify away from TSMC for some components, TSMC would retain the most critical and complex GPU compute die manufacturing. The deal reflects supply constraints rather than fundamental weakness in TSMC's business.

Analysts expect Apple to use Intel 18A for some M-series chips and potentially Intel 14A for future iPhone chips, but this is speculative and represents a secondary opportunity compared to the Nvidia potential deal.

articles.title: Intel Just Made a Big Bet on ASML's Next-Gen Technology. Here's Why It Matters in 2026.
articles.author: Leo Sun
articles.description: Intel is investing heavily in ASML's high-NA EUV lithography systems to reclaim its process technology lead from TSMC. The company plans to mass-produce its 14A chips in 2027-2028, ahead of TSMC's comparable A14 chips. However, this costly strategy requires Intel to stabilize its high-NA process in 2026 while expanding older nodes. Analysts expect Intel to remain unprofitable in 2026 but turn profitable in 2027 if the bet pays off.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Intel is making a strategic bet on advanced technology that could restore competitiveness, but faces significant execution risk, continued losses in 2026, and high capital expenditures. Success is uncertain and dependent on stabilizing new manufacturing processes.

ASML benefits from Intel's major investment in its high-NA EUV systems, which cost up to $400 million each. As the sole producer of EUV lithography systems, ASML stands to gain significant revenue from both Intel and TSMC's adoption of this technology.

TSMC currently maintains technological leadership but faces potential competition from Intel's earlier adoption of high-NA EUV systems. However, TSMC's cautious approach of maximizing existing low-NA systems until 2030 suggests confidence in its competitive position.

AMD has benefited from Intel's past struggles by gaining market share through TSMC partnerships, but faces potential headwinds if Intel successfully closes the technology gap with its 14A chips in 2027-2028.
